power/measured: Measure the slope of x squared with a tiny step, at a few points: minus three at minus one point five, zero at zero, two at one, and three at one point five.
power/twox: Every one of them is two times x. So the derivative of x squared is two x, at every point, with no limit to take.
power/sq: Write it as x squared becomes two x. The arrow stands for “becomes”, from a function to its derivative. The two came down in front, and the power dropped by one.
power/cube: Do the same to x cubed: bring the three down, and drop the power to two. x cubed becomes three x squared.
power/check: Check it at x equals two. The measured slope of x cubed is twelve, and three times two squared is twelve.
power/rule: In general, for any power n, x to the n becomes n times x to the n minus one. That is the power rule.
sums/factor: A number in front comes along for the ride. Five x cubed becomes five times three x squared: fifteen x squared.
sums/sum: A sum is differentiated one term at a time. Two x is a line with slope two.
sums/zero: A constant on its own is flat, so its derivative is zero. The seven drops out.
sums/whole: So five x cubed plus two x plus seven has derivative fifteen x squared plus two.
explog/ex: e to the x is special: it is its own derivative. At every point, its slope equals its height.
explog/eax: Now put a three in the power. Each step in x moves the power three times as far, and the measured slope of e to the three x at zero is three, where its height is one.
explog/one: At x equals one, the height is twenty point oh nine, and the slope is about sixty point three: three times the height again.
explog/rule: So the three comes out in front: e to the three x becomes three e to the three x. For any number a, e to the a x becomes a times e to the a x.
explog/ln: And ln x has derivative one over x: steep near zero, flatter as x grows. At x equals two, its slope is a half.
try/p1: Try a mix: f of x equals two x cubed, plus four e to the minus two x, minus three ln x. Take it one term at a time.
try/t1: Two x cubed: the three comes down, and three times two is six. Six x squared.
try/t2: Four e to the minus two x: the minus two in the power comes out in front. Four times minus two is minus eight, so minus eight e to the minus two x.
try/t3: Three ln x has derivative three over x. It is subtracted, so its derivative is too: minus three over x.
try/sum: Together, f prime of x is six x squared, minus eight e to the minus two x, minus three over x.
try/p2: Now a slope at one point. For f of x equals x squared plus six ln x, what is f prime of two?
try/a2: Differentiate first: two x, plus six over x. Then put in two: four plus three, seven.
